title: feat: add gt commit and file filters for diffs
body:
`gt` could not look at commits: no listing, no single commit, no diff of one, no statuses, so reading history on the server meant `gt api` or a clone.

`gt commit` reads the repository on the server, with the SDK's commit endpoints:

- `list [<ref>]` (`--path`, `--not`, `--limit`, `--page`), `view <ref>`, `diff <ref>`, `compare <base>...<head>`, `status <ref>` and `pr <sha>`. A ref is a SHA, branch or tag.
- The additions, deletions, files and signature check of `--json` cost the server extra work and are read only when the output includes them.
- `status` exits 1 when a status failed and 8 while one is pending, like `gt pr checks`, so `gt commit status main && deploy` waits for green.

Diffs get filters like the file tree of the web interface. Gitea's API takes no options for what a diff contains (whitespace included), so they work on the diff once it is read, and what is left is still a diff that `git apply` takes:

- `--path` and `--exclude` take a file, a `dir/` or a glob (`*.go`, `internal/**/*_test.go`), repeatable.
- `--name-only`, `--name-status` and `--stat` summarize it.
- `gt commit diff` and `gt pr diff` share them; `commit diff --patch` writes the patch `git am` takes.

Tried against gitea.com for every subcommand. Writing statuses and tags are left for other changes.
